mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns, so that the current low rate (0.38%) predicts positive returns. The signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 240 indicates elevated inflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to central bank tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL>240), or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 and unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 tends to have positive 20-day forward returns due to strong economic growth and rising corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO<105 AND UNRATE<4.5, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS and other indicators), the S&P 500 tends to have negative 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates and reduced risk tolerance.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST index above 1100 indicates strong housing market activity, which is associated with positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to robust economic growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (HOUST>1100), or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1100 and residential investment (RSAFS) exceed 450000, the S&P 500 tends to have positive 60-day forward returns due to sustained economic expansion and rising corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST>1100 AND RSAFS>450000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (as indicated by high GDP growth and other indicators), the S&P 500 tends to have negative 20-day forward returns due to elevated risk of recession and central bank tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of employment (PAYEMS) is positively related to S&P 500 5-day forward returns, so that the current high employment (143560) predicts positive returns. The signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above 140000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.
